text:
maya: Heads-up — new token-level dashboard is showing a persistent 99p spike for /chat-stream since the kernel-selector heuristic change rolled last night. Looks correlated with MIG slices 2 and 3 being hotter than the others.

devin: Yep saw that. 99p token latency jumped ~40ms on that route. I pulled traces, KV cache hit-rate is same, but SM occupancy distribution shifted.

maya: Attaching the grafana query I'm using to slice by route + mig_slice: 
```
sum by(status_code, route, mig_slice) (rate(redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket{le!="+Inf"}[5m]))
```
Not perfect but gives the percentile heatmap per slice.

jorge: Perf-bot just generated an automated alert: `token_latency.99p > 300ms for route=/chat-stream and mig_slice in (2,3)` —alert fired 1894999800.

perf-bot: (system) Alert details: runbook: runtime/perf/mig-skew. Metrics: `redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket`, `gpu_sm_occupancy_percent`, `gpu_vram_utilization_bytes`.

li: Quick check from the node: `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` snapshot at 1894999900 shows slice 2/3 SM% ~ 88-92 while slice 0/1 ~ 60-68. VRAM per-mig slice is roughly even. Power/thermal stable.

devin: Interesting — kernel-selector changed kernel preference to `matmul_fused_v2` for sequences > 1024 by default. That kernel has slightly different per-warp occupancy behavior which could interact badly with MIG slice scheduling for small batches. I wonder if continuous batcher produced more small-batch churn around that route.

maya: I ran a small traffic replay against the routing policy and toggled the heuristic flag. With `kernel_selector: prefer_legacy=false` we reproduce the spike. With `prefer_legacy=true` 99p drops back ~35ms.

jorge: Can you paste the minimal cfg you toggled?

maya: Sure: 
```yaml
runtime: 
  kernel_selector: 
    prefer_legacy: true # rollback flag
  batching: 
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
    microbatch_timeout_ms: 6
    prefer_latency: true
```

li: Also noticed kvcache prefetches had a short burst at the same time (micro-prefetcher rate doubled). Might be correlated: prefetcher triggers create extra small kernel launches which bump SM occupancy on those slices.

devin: That explains it. If prefetcher + new kernel = extra small kernels that get pinned to same MIG slice(s), we can see skew. We should instrument per-kernel launch counts per-mig-slice. I added a counter: `gpu_kernel_launchs_total{kernel="matmul_fused_v2",mig_slice="X"}`.

maya: Nice. The new counter shows slice 2 has 3x more small launches for `matmul_fused_v2` than slice 0.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary toggle `kernel_selector.prefer_legacy=true` deployed to 10% of dedicated pool at 1895000300.

devin: For the dashboard, I created a compact panel that overlays: token 50/95/99 percentiles, SM occupancy p50/p95, and `kernel_launch_rate` by slice. PromQL used: 
```
# 99p token latency per route per slice
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/chat-stream"}[5m])) by (le, mig_slice))
```

maya: Also added a heatmap that shows "slice skew score" = (sm_p95_by_slice / mean_sm_p95_all_slices) to quickly flag imbalanced machines.

jorge: Action items:
- Rollback kernel-selector globally for the affected fleet while we root cause (devin).
- Add kernel launch per-slice instrumentation to telemetry (devin + li).
- Tune kvcache prefetcher threshold to avoid bursts on hot routes (maya).
- Add alert to detect slice_skew_score > 1.3 for > 5m (sre-ally).

devin: I'm pushing a fix: limit `kvcache.prefetch_max_inflight=8` on hot-route profiles and add a sampler that tags traces with `mig_slice` so we can correlate per-request. Pushed a PR, will run canary before global rollout.

li: Quick note on dashboards: to reduce noise we sample token-level histograms at 1/10 for low QPS routes and keep full fidelity for top 20 routes. Sampling config: `telemetry.histogram_sample_rate_per_route: 0.1` for low volume. This keeps storage cost down and still surfaces per-route regressions.

perf-bot: (system) New dashboard panel published: `runtime/perf/mig_slice_skew_v1` with panels: token-percentiles-by-slice, kernel-launchs-by-slice, kv-prefetch-rate, slice-skew-heatmap.

maya: Canary rollback looks good — 99p normalized on canary machines. Will coordinate global rollback after PR merges.

jorge: Long term we might want kernel-aware packing that spreads small kernel launches across slices; scheduler change rather than kernel swap. Add to roadmap.

sre-ally: I'll add the alert rule to prometheus: 
```yaml
- alert: MIGSliceSkewHigh
  expr: avg_over_time((gpu_sm_occupancy_percent_p95_by_slice / avg(gpu_sm_occupancy_percent_p95_by_node))[5m]) > 1.3
  for: 5m
  labels: {severity: "page"}
  annotations: {runbook: "/runbooks/runtime/mig-skew.md"}
```

devin: TL;DR — kernel selector change + prefetch bursts -> disproportionate small kernel launches on 2 slices -> SM occupancy skew -> token-99p latency spike for /chat-stream. Canary rollback and kvcache throttle look like mitigation.

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll post a short incident note in `incidents/` and we can follow up with perf regression test in CI for `matmul_fused_v2` + prefetch combos. :thumbsup:

sre-ally: Filed: INC-2026, assigned to dev perf team.
